content: Chlorhexidine gluconate is a topical antibacterial agent approved by the FDA for specific uses, including the treatment of gingivitis and periodontitis, as well as for skin cleansing procedures. It is commonly used as a surgical hand scrub, a handwash for healthcare personnel, a preoperative skin preparation for patients, and for general skin and wound cleansing. When used as a surgical hand scrub, the process involves wetting the hands and forearms under running water for 30 seconds, cleaning the fingernails with a nail stick or similar tool, and scrubbing for 1.5 minutes with approximately 8 mL of the product. This can be done with or without a wet brush, ensuring attention to the nails, cuticles, and skin between the fingers. The hands are then rinsed thoroughly under running water for 30 seconds, followed by an additional 1.5-minute wash with 8 mL of the product, and a final rinse for 30 seconds. The hands should be dried thoroughly afterward. For healthcare personnel handwashing, the hands are first wet with water, and about 5 mL of the product is dispensed into cupped hands. The hands are washed vigorously for 15 seconds, then rinsed and dried thoroughly. For preoperative skin preparation, the product is applied liberally to the surgical site and swabbed for at least 2 minutes. The area is then dried with a sterile towel. This procedure is repeated for an additional 2 minutes, followed by drying with a sterile towel. For general skin and wound cleansing, the area to be cleaned is first rinsed thoroughly with water. A minimal amount of the product is applied to cover the skin or wound area, and the area is washed gently. The site is then rinsed thoroughly again. Adverse reactions associated with the use of chlorhexidine gluconate include staining of teeth and other oral surfaces, the formation of calculus, alterations in taste perception, headaches, and in rare cases, anaphylaxis. This product is intended for external use only and should be kept out of the reach of children. If swallowed, immediate medical attention or contact with a Poison Control Center is necessary. There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of chlorhexidine gluconate in pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no guidance on its use in specific gender or racial populations, or in immunocompromised patients. The product should be stored at a temperature of 20-25°C (68-77°F) and should not be exposed to excessive heat above 40°C (104°F). The interaction between alcohol and chlorhexidine gluconate has not been established, and patients are advised to consult their healthcare provider regarding the use of alcohol while using this medication.
